title: Measure Domain’s Gap: A Similar Domain Selection Principle for Multi-Domain Recommendation

problem.claim: Unselective transfer of information from all domains can cause negative transfer when domains conflict or have poor quality.

gap.claim: Existing multi-domain recommendation methods generally use a single structure for transferring complex domain-shared knowledge and do not adequately model complex transfer relationships between domains.

contributions.claim: A dynamic Similar Domain Selection Principle is proposed to select suitable domain knowledge for each domain.
A prototype-based domain distance measure is proposed to model relationships between domains.
The principle dynamically selects similar domains using supervised domain-metric signals and an unsupervised distance measure derived from learned domain prototypes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first solution in multi-domain recommendation to explicitly measure domain-level gaps and dynamically select appropriate domains.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.
The authors report that the method is lightweight, can be incorporated into existing multi-domain recommendation methods, and does not introduce excessive time overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-domain recommendation uses transfer information across domains to improve recommendation performance.
Existing approaches transfer complex shared knowledge through a single structure, although useful transfer varies by domain and indiscriminate transfer can cause negative transfer.
Modeling complex transfer relationships between domains remains unresolved.
The proposed principle measures domain distance and dynamically selects similar domains using domain metrics and learned prototypes.
The authors report lightweight integration and effectiveness results from experiments on three datasets.

source_observation.claim: Transfer usefulness varies across domains, and indiscriminate transfer can produce negative transfer.

interpretation.claim: Transfer mechanisms should account for domain-specific compatibility rather than assume that all source domains are beneficial.

application.claim: Use domain-level similarity or distance signals to select transfer sources dynamically.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that dynamic domain selection is beneficial for domains or settings beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the prototype-learning procedure or the supervised domain metrics in detail.
The abstract does not establish the computational overhead quantitatively.
